questions.stem: In a galvanic (voltaic) cell, which electrode undergoes oxidation?

options.option_text: The anode — oxidation occurs at the anode; it is the negative terminal in a galvanic cell
The cathode — reduction occurs at the cathode; it is the positive terminal
Both electrodes oxidise simultaneously in a galvanic cell at once (not this)
Neither electrode; oxidation only occurs in electrolytic cells, not galvanic

questions.explanation: GALVANIC CELL: ANODE = oxidation (OIL) = negative terminal; electrons flow OUT. CATHODE = reduction (RIG) = positive terminal; electrons flow IN. Mnemonic: AN OX / RED CAT. CONTRAST with ELECTROLYTIC CELL: anode is POSITIVE (connected to +ve terminal of battery). DANIELL CELL: Zn (anode) oxidised; Cu deposited at cathode. PYQ: anode/cathode + oxidation/reduction in IBPS PO, SSC CGL chemistry.

questions.stem: According to Faraday's First Law of Electrolysis, the mass of substance deposited at an electrode is:

options.option_text: Directly proportional to the quantity of charge passed (m proportional to Q)
Inversely proportional to the charge — higher charge deposits less substance instead
Proportional to the square of the current applied to the electrode only
Independent of charge; it depends only on electrode surface area alone

questions.explanation: FARADAY FIRST LAW: m = Z x Q = Z x I x t; where Z = electrochemical equivalent, I = current (A), t = time (s). m is proportional to Q (charge). FARADAY SECOND LAW: for same charge, masses of different substances are proportional to their equivalent weights (M/n). FARADAY CONSTANT: F = 96,500 C/mol. ELECTROPLATING: silver plating — 107.9 g Ag deposited per 96,500 C. PYQ: Faraday first law in IBPS PO/SSC hybrid sections.

questions.stem: The standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) is assigned a standard reduction potential of:

options.option_text: 0.00 V — it is the reference electrode against which all other potentials are measured
+1.00 V — this is approximately the reduction potential of oxygen, not SHE
-1.00 V — a negative potential would mean SHE oxidises readily; it is defined as zero
+0.76 V — this is the reduction potential of Zn2+/Zn couple, not SHE

questions.explanation: SHE: H+(1M) + e- → 1/2 H2 at 25°C, 1 atm. E° = 0.00 V BY DEFINITION. All standard reduction potentials measured relative to SHE. ELECTROCHEMICAL SERIES: metals with E° < 0 (Zn = -0.76V, Fe = -0.44V) are stronger reducing agents. Metals with E° > 0 (Cu = +0.34V, Ag = +0.80V) are less reactive. CELL EMF = E°cathode - E°anode. Daniell cell: E° = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10V. PYQ: SHE reference + cell EMF in CBSE/IBPS PO.

questions.stem: During the electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid using platinum electrodes, which gas is liberated at the cathode?

options.option_text: Hydrogen (H2) — reduction of H+ ions at cathode: 2H+ + 2e- yields H2
Oxygen (O2) — oxygen is liberated at the ANODE, not the cathode
Sulphur dioxide (SO2) — sulphate ions are not discharged under these conditions
No gas; platinum electrodes absorb all products during electrolysis

questions.explanation: ELECTROLYSIS OF DILUTE H2SO4: CATHODE (reduction): 2H+ + 2e- → H2. ANODE (oxidation): 2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e-. GAS RATIO: H2:O2 = 2:1 by volume. NET: 2H2O → 2H2 + O2. HOFFMAN VOLTAMETER: lab apparatus; hydrogen at cathode is double the volume of oxygen at anode. ELECTROLYSIS OF BRINE: cathode = H2; anode = Cl2; NaOH in solution (chlor-alkali process). PYQ: electrode products in electrolysis — SSC CGL, IBPS PO 1-2x per cycle.

questions.stem: Corrosion of iron (rusting) is an electrochemical process. Which condition MOST accelerates rusting?

options.option_text: Presence of both water and oxygen together — neither alone causes significant rusting
Exposure to oxygen alone in completely dry conditions causes fastest rusting
Immersion in pure distilled water with no dissolved oxygen or salts present
Exposure to nitrogen gas, which reacts with iron to form iron nitride instead

questions.explanation: RUSTING: requires BOTH water AND oxygen. MECHANISM: Fe acts as anode (Fe → Fe2+ + 2e-); dissolved O2 in water acts as cathode. ACCELERATED BY: salt water (more electrolyte), acid rain, contact with dissimilar metals (galvanic corrosion). PREVENTION: painting, galvanising (Zn coating = sacrificial anode), cathodic protection, alloying (stainless steel = Fe+Cr+Ni). GALVANISING: Zn oxidises first even if coating scratches (more reactive than Fe). PYQ: rusting conditions + prevention in UPSC, SSC, IBPS GA.

questions.stem: How much silver (atomic mass 108 g/mol) is deposited when 2A is passed through silver nitrate solution for 965 seconds? (F = 96,500 C/mol)

options.option_text: 4.32 g — doubles the correct answer, likely from using charge = 2 x 965 x 2 incorrectly
1.08 g — halves the correct answer; miscounts the charge or misapplies valency
21.6 g — moves the decimal wrongly in the moles calculation step (not this)

questions.explanation: FARADAY FIRST LAW CALCULATION: Q = I x t = 2 x 965 = 1930 C. Moles of electrons = Q/F = 1930/96500 = 0.02 mol. Ag+ + e- → Ag (valency = 1). Moles Ag = 0.02 mol. Mass = 0.02 x 108 = 2.16 g. VERIFICATION: 96500 C deposits 108 g Ag. 1930 C deposits (1930/96500) x 108 = 2.16 g. Ratio: 1930/96500 = 1/50; 108/50 = 2.16 check complete.

questions.stem: The Nernst equation modifies the standard EMF of a cell to account for:

options.option_text: The actual concentrations of ions in solution (non-standard conditions)
The temperature of the electrodes, assuming ion concentrations are always standard
The physical size of the electrodes and their surface area for reaction only
The voltage loss due to internal resistance of the electrolyte in solution

questions.explanation: NERNST EQUATION: E = E° - (0.0592/n) log Q at 25°C. Q = reaction quotient (actual concentrations). PURPOSE: calculates actual cell EMF when concentrations differ from 1M standard. CONCENTRATION CELL: two half-cells of same element at different concentrations → EMF from concentration gradient only (E° = 0). APPLICATION: pH meter works on Nernst principle. At EQUILIBRIUM: E = 0; then log K = nE°/0.0592 → links EMF to equilibrium constant. PYQ: Nernst equation concept in UPSC GS-1, IBPS PO advanced science.
